title: Tenant SLA-aware soft quotas with probabilistic demotion for hosted spillover
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: When dedicated pools saturate we currently fall back to hosted capacity using hard rules that either (a) immediate redirect or (b) strict FIFO backfill. This causes unpredictable latency spikes, cost overruns for tenants, and cache inefficiency because KV caches for dedicated variants are not always compatible with hosted variants. Goal: Design and implement a soft-quota + probabilistic demotion mechanism that preserves tenant SLAs where possible, minimizes cost delta on hosted spillover, and keeps KV cache hit-rates acceptable during degradations. The mechanism should be tenant-aware (SLA tier, burst history, remaining quota), model-aware (compatibility score between variant pairs), and cache-aware (KV prefix compatibility).
acceptance_criteria: Configurable soft-quota per tenant that reduces probability of immediate hosted spillover above threshold
Demotion decision function that returns a probability p(hosted) and logs rationale for traceability
Integration test harness simulating multi-tenant burst scenarios with metrics for latency P50/P95/P99, cost delta, and KV cache hit-rate
Canary rollout to 10% of production tenants with automatic rollback if P99 latency increases > 20% or error-rate increases > 2x
Dashboard with per-tenant soft-quota burn rate, hosted-fallback-rate, average compatibility score, and expected vs observed cost impact
notes: Design principle: favor short, probabilistic routing decisions that smooth load rather than large blunt preemption waves
Compatibility score: cosine(similarity of tokenizer prefix distributions, KV cache key namespace overlap, and model family) normalized 0..1
Soft-quotas are not hard caps — they control Poisson thinning (probability) to route to hosted to avoid sharp step functions
Grace credits: tenants accumulate short-term burst credits up to X tokens/min for 5 minutes; credits are decayed by half-life to avoid long-term accumulation
We should avoid model variant swap for stateful sessions unless compatibility score > 0.8 and KV cache restore confidence > 0.6
Cost control: promise per-tenant projected hosted spend limit and expose opt-in emergency override to SREs
design_alternatives: Backpressure-first: throttle tenant at edge → rejected requests. Pro: immediate cost control. Con: poor UX for paid tiers
Strict priority reserve: reserve fractional dedicated capacity per tenant. Pro: deterministic. Con: inflexible and underutilizes capacity
Model-demote-first: always try a lower-cost quantized variant before hosted fallback. Pro: preserves locality. Con: may reduce quality unexpectedly
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Simulation (2 wks): extend load simulator to model tenant burst profiles and KV cache overlap. Metrics produced: P99 latency, hosted fallback rate, cache hit-rate. Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-sim PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-sim/pull/78

Phase 2 - Scoring service (3 wks): standalone compatibility scorer service that returns model-variant compatibility and expected KV restore cost. Endpoint: /v1/compatibility. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compatibility-svc/pull/12

Phase 3 - Router integration (4 wks): integrate probabilistic demotion hook in edge router; add tenant soft-quota config in tenant metadata and decision logging in tracing layer. Feature flag rollout via config service. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/419
Phase 4 - Canary + Monitoring (2 wks): roll to 10% tenants, monitor dashboards and alert thresholds; gather feedback and iterate
Phase 5 - Full rollout and playbook update (1 wk): update runbook for SRE and support with emergency opt-outs and cost reconciliation steps
